description: Surfaces that the UI/UX scoring programme must capture. Derived from the App Router tree (src/app/**/page.tsx) and the workspace registry (GITHUB_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_MAPPINGS in src/lib/github-project-sync.ts). Verified by scripts/derive-captured-surfaces.ts, which fails when the app serves a route this file does not list, when a capture decision is missing or unrecognised, when an exclusion is unjustified or unattributed, when a 'required' surface has never actually been captured, and -- since #147 -- when a capture has gone STALE because the files that render that surface changed after it was measured. See mission-control-kanban#142, #144 and #147.

captureContract.required: The surface is in the scoring programme. It must carry a 'capturedAt' record naming the 40-hex commit measured, the ISO date, the viewport labels covered, the method used, and the 'sourceDigest' of the files that render it -- or an explicit 'captureDeferred' with a substantive reason and a tracking issue. 'required' with neither is a NON-passing state: the surface is unmeasured, not known-good.
captureContract.excluded: The surface is deliberately outside the programme. It must carry a substantive 'reason' (>= 20 chars, no placeholders) and an 'excludedBy' tracking reference (#issue, URL, or 40-hex commit) so the downgrade is attributable and reviewable.
captureContract.capture: npm run surfaces:probe -- measures element-level clipping. Document scroll is NOT a valid measurement here: src/app/globals.css clamps html/body with max-width:100vw and overflow-x:hidden, so an overflowing page reports zero document scroll. Recording a capture is deliberately a manual edit: 'npm run surfaces:fingerprint' only prints, so nobody can re-green a stale capture without touching the same block that holds the date and the method.
captureContract.sourceDigest: A 16-hex content fingerprint over the transitive static local-import closure of the files that render this surface: the route's page, every layout/template that wraps it, everything they import through '@/' or a relative path, and the styling config (tailwind.config.ts, postcss.config.mjs). Print the current value with 'npm run surfaces:fingerprint'. The gate recomputes it and fails when it moved, so a capture cannot keep reading as evidence after the surface has been rewritten. It is CONTENT, not ancestry: a rebase or a re-land that reproduces identical files keeps the capture valid, and a rewrite that keeps the same sha does not. Line endings are normalised to LF first, because this repo has core.autocrlf=true and no .gitattributes. Resolution rules and the list of what this deliberately does NOT cover -- npm dependency bumps, runtime/env-dependent content, API route handlers, next.config.mjs, public assets -- are documented at the top of scripts/surface-dependencies.ts. Bumping DEPENDENCY_CONTRACT_VERSION there invalidates every capture on purpose.

surfaces.note: Global settings. The first ever capture (2026-08-13, e50e256) found 17 clipped elements at 1440px (0 at 390px) in the RuntimeConfigTemplateGallery env-diagnostic badges; #145. Fixed in d677d1cd2221369e0ba4b52047b7e7315a8a221a (min-w-0 + break-all on the badge). This surface's badge content is env-dependent (it renders whatever MCK_* vars resolve on the measuring host), so the fix was additionally checked against synthetic env names of 27/60/120/240 chars: 0px badge-row overflow at every length with the fix, and 46/244/604/1324px with the two classes removed. That env-dependence is a known blind spot of sourceDigest, which covers source only. The 2026-08-13 capture of this surface was superseded by the #145 fix; re-probed at 8f72854 on 2026-08-16 alongside the other eight: 0 clipped elements at both viewports.

capturedAt.method: scripts/probe-surface-clipping.mjs (element-level clipping; 0 clipped at both viewports; self-proof injection moved clipped 0->1 while document overflow stayed 0)
